### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **49** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**57** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed906d567acc09c68812fa36bcdabc873a3fbbef`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed906d567acc09c68812fa36bcdabc873a3fbbef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `73e67454c07500c77651ea1ee377fbdc74e15592` — the merge of head `06d62d2d7cd9a7d201ad96cdc2b3ec9484593dce` into base `ed906d567acc09c68812fa36bcdabc873a3fbbef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 73e67454c07500c77651ea1ee377fbdc74e15592 && git checkout 73e67454c07500c77651ea1ee377fbdc74e15592
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed906d567acc09c68812fa36bcdabc873a3fbbef 06d62d2d7cd9a7d201ad96cdc2b3ec9484593dce && git checkout -B drift-repro ed906d567acc09c68812fa36bcdabc873a3fbbef && git merge --no-ff 06d62d2d7cd9a7d201ad96cdc2b3ec9484593dce

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed906d567acc09c68812fa36bcdabc873a3fbbef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed906d567acc09c68812fa36bcdabc873a3fbbef` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：系统设置里新增"工作日历"和"日历例外日期"两个页面：管理员可以设定每周上班时间、标记默认日历、录入节假日和调休上班日，也可以批量导入；列表里会提示哪些日历快到维护期限。
- 为什么做：工作日历这张卡的第二半，给上一半的计算提供数据；两半同批上线。
- 出错会怎样：日历录错会让按工作日算出的期限不对；录入时会拦下跨午夜、时段重叠等明显错误。
- 要你做什么：无。席位做合同复审；第一半合并后，这一半改成以主干为基础再合并。
- 席位意见：通过；等检查全部跑完全绿后交席位复审。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT, one item before the L2** · head `320ed52d8829c20f16e3862c204c61a0c5b43ced` · Fixes #35355 (PR-B of the split; base `claude/issue-35355-work-calendar-objects-service`, PR-A #35641) · K=11 against `main` · merge-tree with `main` clean · not governed (0 of 45 paths) · 1,806 lines of its own (3,693 cumulative while A is open) · 2026-11-19T21:40Z

**Shape.** Over PR-A's head there are two commits: `c3e3d1be1e` (the change) and `320ed52d88` (A's spec-symbol fix merged in). 45 files:
- the two objects `sys_work_calendar` and `sys_work_calendar_exception` in `packages/platform-objects/src/system/`, with their name constants;
- 11 `*.objects.generated.ts` bundles at 123 lines each, plus source hashes and bundle wiring;
- two `SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` entries;
- the tenancy census, the cli ownership inventory and the cli Setup-tree pin;
- a changeset.

**Claim surface: holds.** Claim 7013077388 names `packages/platform-objects/**`, the spec name constant, the Setup page and import, and the generated translations. Amendment 7021881794 adds the census, the inventory and "the cli Setup-tree pin test", which is `packages/cli/test/connect-agent-both-halves-wire.pin.test.ts`. That pin moves 31 → 33 with a history line and asserts both new nav ids.

**Objects.**
- Both are `managedBy: 'system-data'`. The exception object takes `userActions: { import: true }`, the generic import door per reading A2, and cascades from its calendar.
- `code` is unique per organization and matches `WORK_CALENDAR_CODE_PATTERN`. `timezone` is `required: true` with an IANA value domain. It is filled server-side before validation (see my record on #35641), but the Console form will still demand it: the body's acceptance note on open point 6.
- `needs_maintenance` reads `WORK_CALENDAR_MAINTENANCE_LEAD_DAYS` from spec rather than a literal.

**R1 (before the L2): CI green on this head.** At this reading: 45 success, 11 skipped, and 11 in progress (Test UI 2, 3, 4, 8, 10 and 15 of 16; Test Core 1, 3, 9 and 10 of 10; Type Check · workspace). The PR-body guards ran twice: a `failure` at 21:18:29Z, before re-claim 7022517146, and a `success` at 21:24:55Z, which stands.

**After PR-A lands.** Retarget to `main`. The re-run CI on that base is the head the L2 and the landing read. If the retarget needs more than a fast merge, for example regenerated `api-surface` or `export-origins` because #35581 or #35583 landed first, the new head needs a delta L1.

**Routing.** Clause-② yes (widening), and the spec name constant is a `packages/spec` face: L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by seat 5, together with PR-A. Not governed, so data-1 lands it after A. The semver, P4 and release-coupling notes in my #35641 record apply to the pair.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `320ed52d8829c20f16e3862c204c61a0c5b43ced`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-work-calendar.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-work-calendar-exception.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts

PR #35642 is half B of card #35355 (ADR-0157), stacked on half A (#35641). This record judges B's own increment: the 45-file diff from A's head `ad45d084f4` (the PR base and the merge base) to the head above, the same file list GitHub shows. Half A was read only to check that B's objects agree with the service and write hooks they are judged by. The rest of the diff (tests, the eleven generated bundles and their source-hash files, the locale nav labels, the extract config, the census, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT; the locale bundles were read for structure only, as asked.

Check-runs on this head as read: 59 success, 11 skipped, 1 failure, none in progress. The failure is the first run of `PR-body guards` (check:closing-target-claim, before claim 7022517146 named the setup branch); the same check re-ran on this head and succeeded, so no gate is red.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `sys_work_calendar` and `sys_work_calendar_exception`, in sorted position, so `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` answer for both. Right: both files exist under `packages/platform-objects/src/system/`, which is what the registry's own conformance scan reads.
2. A stack action whose `objectName` is either name is now accepted by `stack.zod.ts` (a platform-prefixed name outside the list is refused there), and the lint ladder resolves a reference to either name. Right, and it is a widening: nothing accepted before is refused.
3. `PlatformObjectsPlugin` registers both objects in its first manifest, unconditionally. Every composition gains two tables on the project database, and both vote in `resolvePrimaryDatasource` beside `sys_exchange_rate`. Right, additive.
4. With the objects registered, half A's service stops answering "no calendar object" and its hooks bind to real declarations. Read in `engine-insert.ts`: defaults, then `beforeInsert` hooks, then record validation, then validation rules. So the hook's time-zone fill runs before `required` is judged, and the code format rule and the `iana_time_zone` domain judge the filled row. Right. Field names agree with what half A reads: `code`, `timezone`, `is_default`, `maintained_from`, `maintained_through`, the seven `*_periods` columns, and `calendar`, `date`, `kind`, `periods` on the exception.
5. Data API: both objects are `apiEnabled` with the `system-data` affordances (create, edit, delete); import is opened on the exception object alone. Right, the `sys_exchange_rate` shape.
6. Accept-sets the objects close: `code` unique per organization and held to the same pattern string the service tests a named code against; one exception row per (calendar, date) per organization (D10); `kind` is `off` or `on` only, which is the pair the exception hook judges. Right. No stored rows exist, so nothing is narrowed.
7. Setup gains two `group_configuration` entries after Exchange Rates, each naming a view its object declares; the Setup-tree pin moves from 31 to 33. Right.
8. `@objectstack/platform-objects` exports `SysWorkCalendar`, `SysWorkCalendarException` and `WORK_CALENDAR_PERIODS_HELP`. Additive.
9. Organization-ownership inventory: two attribution rows, the exception anchored to its calendar through `parent('calendar', 'sys_work_calendar')`. Right: both tables carry `organization_id` (census: 105 registered, 54 in reach).
10. Locales, structure only: each of the eleven `*.objects.generated.ts` files gains 123 lines with a key skeleton identical to English; the literal tokens (`HH:mm-HH:mm`, the example periods, `24:00`, `cn_standard`, `Asia/Shanghai`, `60`) occur the same number of times in every locale; the values left identical to English (2 to 5 per locale, none in Arabic) are exactly the rows added to the source-hash files; both nav labels are present in all eleven locale files. Complete. Prose quality is not judged here.

### ② Semver level

The changeset carries `@objectstack/platform-objects` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/cli` patch, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, and the PR body carries the same two lines. That matches what the diff publishes: the protocol change (two new platform object names an author may now reference) takes minor on the package that ships the objects, and the registry and inventory edits are patch. The three packages named are the three released packages the diff moves.

Clause-②: yes (widening) stands on B's own increment (derived judgments 1 and 2); it does not need half A to be true.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and open questions that reach this half, each answered:

- Required `maintained_through` (open point 2): accepted. D3 says a blank must not read as "no holidays from here on", and a required field is the plainest shape that holds it.
- Required `maintained_from`, a field outside D1's list (past-side bound): accepted. Comment 7005998663 puts refusing like D8 inside the ADR and keeps only "covered by the weekly pattern" out of this card's hands; an explicit bound is the refusing choice.
- Lead time of 60 days: accepted. D8 leaves the distance to this card, and 60 days puts a calendar maintained through 31 December on the list from 1 November.
- Time-zone prefill server-side only (the report's sixth question): not accepted as built. See S1. The half this review can settle is the object's help text; whether a server-side fill alone meets D7 is a ruled sentence and is escalated to the maintainer.
- Where the arithmetic lives, and under whose authority the service reads: half A's, not judged here.
- Files beyond the claimed surface (inventory, census, bundle-ownership list, Setup-tree pin): covered by claim amendment 7021881794.
- Machine-made translations in ten locales: disclosed in the PR body and put to the maintainer there. Structure is complete (derived judgment 10).
- Stacking: the PR is a draft on A's branch and says so. This record covers this head only; if A's head moves and B merges it again, the new head needs its own record.
- Overlap with #35581 and #34223 in the additive lists and the Setup-tree pin: textual, whoever lands second re-counts the pin.
- The PR body's test readings name the previous head; the check-runs on this head are the gate verdicts.

SQL push-down: B adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to find.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`: holds. Both names are real, sit under the package that registers them, and keep the list sorted. The first consumers (the action-reference check in `stack.zod.ts`, the lint ladder, the primary-datasource vote) all read them correctly.

`plugin.ts` and `system/index.ts`: hold. ADR-0157 left the owning package to this card; the choice (platform-objects, first manifest) is argued in the docblock on the `sys_exchange_rate` precedent, and the reader is indeed the engine's service, not one optional plugin.

`organization-ownership-inventory.ts`: holds (derived judgment 9).

`setup-nav.contributions.ts`: holds. The comment's claims (the exception list is the import door, `needs_maintenance` is the D8 notice, access by object grant) match the objects.

`sys-work-calendar-exception.object.ts`: holds against D1 and D10. Checked in the live tree: the import resolver tries the id, the target's title field (`name`) and its unique fields (`code`), so the docblock's "by its code or its name" is true; import writes go through `beforeInsert` hooks even with automations off, because only metadata-bound hooks are skipped; `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` is a declared value; the audit writer works from a skip list that names neither object.

`sys-work-calendar.object.ts`: holds against D1, D2, D3, D8 and D10, with one sentence that does not (S1). Checked: the `format` rule shape and its evaluator; `unique: 'organization'`; the `needs_maintenance` filter (`less_than_or_equal` is a canonical operator, `{60_days_from_now}` is in the date-macro grammar and is resolved on the engine's find path; a calendar already past its date is listed too).

S1 (should-fix) — D7's Setup prefill is not delivered, and the `timezone` help text says something the Setup form refuses. D7 reads "Setup prefills it from the organization's effective time zone", and the card's Scope says "prefilled". At this head the field is `required: true` with no declared default. The Console create form treats that as required (`isRequiredInForm` lowers `required` only for a runtime default) and refuses a blank before any request is sent, so the server-side fill in half A is reachable from an API caller or a seed and never from Setup. The help text, in all eleven locales, tells the administrator "Left out on create, it takes the organization's default time zone". On the form that shows this text, leaving it out is refused. The report's reason for stopping at the server ("no default-token mechanism exists") overlooks the create form's seed context, which already opens a record-currency code field on `localization.currency` (ADR-0144 D8 rule 4, `schemaDefaults.ts`), and `useLocalization()` carries the time zone too. Closed by either of two things: the Setup create form opens with the organization's time zone in the field, which needs a `ui/` change and so a claim amendment; or the maintainer rules that the server-side fill alone meets D7. Either way the help text must end up saying what the Setup form does.

S2 (should-fix) — nothing tests the real objects. Half A's hook tests run on fixtures whose fields are plain text: no `required`, no select, no lookup, no unique key, no format rule. B's tests pin registration, the nav count and bundle ownership. So no test measures a create on the real `sys_work_calendar` that leaves `timezone` out (it depends on hooks running before `required`, which I read but nothing holds), the code-shape refusal, the (calendar, date) key, or the import door on `sys_work_calendar_exception` naming a calendar by code with one bad row refused alone. The card's Done-when asks for the objects, service and Setup page to land with tests, D3's import is this card's to enforce, and the precedent pinned its own import (`packages/rest/src/import-exchange-rate-csv.test.ts`). Closed by one test file that drives the two real objects through a real engine with `installWorkCalendarHooks` bound, covering those four cases.

N1 (nit) — the exception's `periods` help restates the period format by hand and leaves out the same-day and `24:00` sentences, while the calendar file says the format is stated once in `WORK_CALENDAR_PERIODS_HELP`. Left as a follow-up; fixing it here moves the head.

N2 (nit) — `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx` lists what `group_configuration` holds and describes Exchange Rates; the two new Setup pages are not mentioned anywhere an administrator reads. `Skills-docs: none` gives a reason for authors, not for administrators. A follow-up, due with the same release (D4).

N3 (nit) — the D8 notice is a second list view an administrator has to open; nothing marks a calendar near its date on the default `All` view. It meets D8's wording ("marks a calendar ... as needing maintenance"), so it is accepted as built; a row mark on `All` would be the stronger reading.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35355-work-calendar-objects-setup`
Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35642`

**VERDICT: PASS**
